inherits_note: Parent SCN-queens-garden is a container node with no card; limestone and garden vocabulary repeated by value from SCN-rose-tree-yard
form: The sunny far edge of the Queen's garden: a warm south-facing stretch of rough grass at the top of a stone-faced ha-ha, with an old stone gate-pier at one end; beyond the ha-ha the ground runs away in pale haze toward the shore
period: Dream-image of the boundary of an 1860s great-house or college garden: the sunk fence (ha-ha) where tended garden gives way to open country

grows_from.waking_detail: a sunlit corner of a great-house garden beyond the croquet lawn
grows_from.design_growth: The warm, overlooked edge of a grand garden where the grown-ups never go: a ha-ha wall catching full sun, long grass, and an old stone gate-pier topped by a weathered heraldic griffin of the kind carved on Oxford college gates, the stone seed of the dream's Gryphon

dream_design_language: The garden runs out: clipped order stops at a sunlit wall and the land beyond has no detail, only brightness, as though the dream has not built it yet

mucha_design_language.item: Mucha / Art Nouveau at the garden's edge: the gate-pier's faces carved in flowing lily-and-vine relief, its cap a carved round halo disc behind the small stone griffin so the statue sits framed like a Mucha emblem; the ha-ha coping carries a thin inlaid band of gold-and-pastel mosaic; the long grass and moon daisies drift in soft flowing lines; pastel-and-gold haze beyond
mucha_design_language.culture_ref: world.json#WR-010 (Queen's garden listed); cultivation.json#XA-magic-08; SCN-rose-tree-yard mucha_design_language
mucha_design_language.why: Same garden language, thinning out where the garden ends

structure.item: a strip of unmown rough grass about 20 m long and 8 m deep, open to the full sun, where the Gryphon (photoreal CGI griffin, SUP-010 as amended BIB-0027) lies asleep in the sun
a ha-ha along the front edge: a vertical dry-stone retaining wall about 1.5 m high dropping to lower ground, so the view is open with no visible fence
structure.why: Real period garden boundary; puts the shore 'beyond' without joining it

structure.item: a square limestone gate-pier about 2.8 m high at one end of the ha-ha, with a small weathered stone griffin crouched on its cap
structure.culture_ref: world.json#wonderland_real_counterparts cp-court (the adult world as a child meets it)
structure.why: College-gate heraldry a child would have seen in Oxford; the waking image the Gryphon grows from. It is plainly a statue, lichened and worn

structure.item: behind, a clipped yew hedge with an arched opening back to the croquet-ground
structure.why: Continuity of the walk from the croquet-ground

materials.item: honey-coloured limestone, sun-warmed, lichened gold and grey
long summer grass going to seed, pale gold tips, a few moon daisies
materials.why: Unmown edge contrasts with the croquet lawn

details.item: a flat sun-warmed patch of grass pressed down where the Gryphon lies
beyond the ha-ha: open land dropping away into a bright pale haze, a faint line of sea-light at the horizon
details.why: Sets up the walk to the Mock Turtle's shore without mapping a real route

scale_notes.rule: True 1:1 (Alice 135 cm). The Gryphon is a photoreal CGI griffin lying on the grass (SUP-010 as amended BIB-0027; size set by 04-creatures); the grass strip (20 x 8 m) is kept large enough for its full wingspan. The stone griffin on the pier is small (about 60 cm), weathered and plainly a statue, so it never competes with the living creature

negative: no living or moving statue, no giant griffin sculpture, no winged creature in the sky
no cartoon griffin, no human in partial griffin costume; the Gryphon is a photoreal CGI creature; no real eagle or lion
no flat poster illustration, outline graphics or matte-painting finish
no fence, railings or wall that visibly block the view beyond
no buildings, town or sea detail beyond the ha-ha; only haze
no fantasy ruins, no Greek temple
prompt_ready_en: the sunlit edge of a formal English garden in midsummer, a strip of long golden grass at the top of a honey-coloured dry-stone ha-ha wall, a thin gold-and-pastel mosaic band along its coping, an old square limestone gate-pier carved in flowing Art Nouveau lily-and-vine relief with a small weathered lichened stone griffin on its cap framed by a carved round halo disc, a clipped yew hedge behind, beyond the ha-ha the land falls away into bright pale pastel-and-gold haze with a faint line of sea-light on the horizon, photographed live-action
